request.notes: Two request shapes. The canonical one is Lens's own SERVICE registration, once at startup (type web-ui); metadata is accepted upstream but never sent. The `human_operator` variant is the operator-identity registration that precedes an identity's first write (REQUIREMENTS §5C.5): id + type="human" and no name, so the row says what the id is rather than inventing a person's name for it. Re-registering an EXISTING id with a type overwrites that agent's stored type and un-archives it, which is why the variant is only ever sent for an id the impersonation guard has cleared through lithos_agent_info.

observed_divergences: The response carries no error envelope in the source, and Lens's two callers treat a failure as a boolean rather than a code: the startup registration is best-effort (register_agent -> False) and the operator registration refuses the write behind it (register_operator -> False, "could not register the operator identity; nothing was changed"). No conditional/create-only form exists, so the lookup -> register window the guard leaves open cannot be closed client-side; recorded as a known limit in docs/SPECIFICATION.md (PRD clarification 3, Dave 2026-10-03).
